senses: to cast, hurl, throw; send away, export
to give leave, give up, allow, suffer, grant, permit, surrender, let
la:verb:permitto.html:
per-mitto, mīsi, missum, 3, v. a.,
to let go through, suffer to pass through.
Lit. (very rare): fenestellae permittant columbas ad introitum exitumque, . —
Transf., to let go, let loose: equos permittunt in hostem,i. e. ride at full speed,: equum concitatum ad hostium aciem, Sisenn. ap. : se incautius in hostem,i. e. to rush upon,: multi ex summo se permitterent, sprang down, Sisenn. ap. : gregem campo,to turn out into,.—Mid., to spread, extend, reach: odor possit permitti longius, spreads farther, Lucr 4, 688: deserta regio ad Arimphaeos usque permittitur,extends,.—
In partic.
To send away, export: caseos trans maria,.—
To let fly, cast, hurl, throw, so as to reach the mark: saxum permittit in hostem,; : longius tela,: quācumque datur permittere visus,to direct, cast,.—
Trop.
To let loose, let go (rare): tribunatum,to make free use of, exercise without reserve,: se ad aliquam rem,to strive after a thing,: habenas equo,.—
To give up, leave, intrust, surrender, commit (class.; syn.: committo, commendo): totum ei negotium permisi,: permittitur infinita potestas,: aliquem judicum potestati,: alicui summam belli administrandi,: fortunas suas fidei alicujus,: alicui licentiam agendarum rerum,: permissum ipsi erat, faceret, quod vellet,: aliquem vitae,to give one his life,: feminas maribus,: permittere se, to give up or surrender one's self: se suaque omnia in fidem atque potestatem populi Romani permittere,: se suaque omnia eorum potestati permittere,; : se in deditionem consulis,; —
To give leave, let, allow, suffer, grant, permit (class.; syn.: sino, patior): neque discessisset a me, nisi ego ei permisissem,: tibi permitto respondere, ne, etc.,: quis Antonio permisit, ut, etc.,: ipsis judicibus conjecturam facere,; : ibi permisso, ut, etc.,; : ut tuto transire permittatur,: permissus ut regnaret,; ; : non permittitur reprimere impetum,: si conjectare permittitur,: permittere sibi, with a foll. object-clause, to allow or permit one's self, to venture to do a thing, .— So with acc.: nil non permittit mulier sibi, Juv 6, 457: permitto aliquid iracundiae tuae,to make allowance for,: inimicitias sibi cum aliquo susceptas patribus conscriptis et temporibus rei publicae,to sacrifice them to the state of the country,.—Hence, permis-sus, a, um, P. a.
Permitted; hence, subst.: permissum, i, n., a permission: utor permisso,; ; .—
Let go, Plaut. ap. Müll.

la:verb:permuto.gloss: to change or alter throughout or completely, transform
senses: to change or alter throughout or completely, transform
to interchange or exchange something for another, swap; exchange money, buy
la:verb:permuto.html:
per-mūto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To change throughout, to alter or change completely: sententiam,: omnem rei publicae statum,: ordine permutato,.—
In gen., to interchange, exchange one thing for another: nomina inter se,: domum,: galeam,: cur valle permutem Sabinā Divitias operosiores?: cum jecore locum,: virus ut hoc alio fallax permutet odore,: plumbum gemmis,for precious stones,.—Trop.: permutatā ratione,on the contrary, conversely,.—
In partic., in the lang. of business.
To exchange money: placuit denarium sedecim assibus permutari,.—Esp. of payments by exchange: illud, quod tecum permutavi,what you remitted to me by bill of exchange,: ait se curasse, ut cum quaestu populi permutaretur,: sed quaero, quod illi opus erit Athenis, permutari ne possit, an ipsi ferendum sit,: velim cures, ut permutetur, Athenas, quod sit in annum sumptum ei,.—
To buy: equos talentis auri permutare,: serichatum permutatur in libras denariis sex,; .—
To turn about, turn round (post.-Aug.): arborem in contrarium,; .

la:verb:permaneo.gloss: to stay to the end, hold out
senses: to stay to the end, hold out
to last, continue, remain, endure, abide, persist, persevere
to devote one's life to, live by
la:verb:permaneo.html:
per-mănĕo, mansi, mansum, 2, v. n.,
to stay to the end; to hold out, last, continue, endure, remain; to persist, persevere (class.; syn.: persto, persevero).
Absol.: ut quam maxime permaneant diuturna corpora,; : ira tam permansit diu,; : Athenis jam ille mos a Cecrope permansit,.—With ad: verris octo mensium incipit salire: permanet, ut id recte facere possit, ad trimum,: perdiuturna, permanens ad longinquum et immensum paene tempus,; so, ad posteros nostros, Decret. Tergest. 2, 26: solus ad extremos permanet ille rogos,: ad numerum,.— With in and acc.: ultima quae mecum seros permansit in annos,.— With adv. quo: quo neque permaneant animae neque corpora nostra,; v. Lachm. ad h. l.—
With in and abl.: Seleucus in maritimā orā permanens,: in voluntate,: in pristinā sententiā,: in proposito susceptoque consilio,: in officio,.—*
With gen.: virtus sola permanet tenoris sui,.—
To abide in a way, rule, or mode of life, to live by, to devote one's life to (eccl. Lat.): in proposito cordis,: in gratiā Dei,: in fide,: in peccato,: in carne,: in eādem regulā,.

la:adj:permultus.html:
per-multus, a, um, adj.,
very much, very many (class.): nescio quantulum attulerit; verum haud permultum attulit,: imitatores,: colles,: permultum erit ex maerore tuo diminutum,: permultum interest, utrum, etc.,: permulta rogatus Fecit,.—Hence, adv.
permultō, very much, by far: permulto clariora,: permulta mihi recurrunt,.—
permultum, very much: permultum ante,very frequently before,.

la:verb:permano.gloss: to flow or leak through; to permeate
senses: to flow or leak through; to permeate
la:verb:permano.html:
per-māno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.,
to flow through, press through, penetrate.
Lit. (rare): in saxis ac speluncis permanat aquarum Liquidus umor,: permanat calor argentum,: primordia singula per quojusque foramina permanare,; so ; .—
Transf., to flow to any place; to penetrate, reach anywhere (class.; syn.: penetro, pervado): sucus permanat ad jecur,: venenum in omnis partis corporis permanat, (but in , the correct read. is permaneant; v. Lachm. ad h. l., and permaneo, α).—
Trop.
To penetrate, reach, extend to any place: amor usque in pectus permanavit,; : conclusiunculae ad sensus non permanantes,: ut sermones hominum ad vestras aures permanarent,: macula permanat ad animum,: Pythagorae doctrina permanavisse mihi videtur in hanc civitatem,; cf.: hoc ubi uno auctore ad plures permanaverat, etc.,.—*
Permanare palam, to be divulged, become known, .

la:adj:permolestus.html:
per-mŏlestus, a, um, adj.,
very troublesome: atque hi non sunt permolesti,.—Adv.: permŏlestē, with much trouble or difficulty: permoleste ferre aliquid,to be much vexed at a thing,; .

la:adj:permagnus.html:
per-magnus, a, um, adj.,
very great, very large: accessio,: vis naturae,: hereditas,: numerus,.— As subst.: permagnum, i, n., a verygreat thing, something very great: permagnum existimans tris Olympionicas unā e domo prodire,: permagni interest,: permagni refert,; so in tmesi: per enim magni aestimo tibi factum nostrum probari,: decumas permagno vendere,at a very high price,.

la:noun:permansio.html:
permansĭo, ōnis, f.
permaneo
,
a remaining, persisting (good prose): numquam laudata est in unā sententiā perpetua permansio,: perseverantia est in ratione bene consideratā stabilis et perpetua permansio,; .

la:verb:permisceo.gloss: to mix or mingle together thoroughly, commingle, intermingle, combine
senses: to mix or mingle together thoroughly, commingle, intermingle, combine
to mix together, unite, join, combine
to throw into confusion, confound, disturb
la:verb:permisceo.html:
per-misceo, scŭi, stum, and xtum, 2, v. a.,
to mix or mingle together; to commingle, intermingle.
Lit.: naturam cum materiā,: permixti cum suis fugientibus,: permixtum senatui populi concilium,: equites turbae hostium,: fructus acerbitate permixti,; : generique cruorem Sanguine cum soceri permiscuit impius ensis,: omnes in oratione esse quasi permixtos et confusos pedes,: (gagates lapis) medetur strumis cerae permixtus,: corpora viva permista sepultis,: alicui totum ensem,to plunge his whole sword into his body,.—
Trop.
In gen., to mix or mingle together; to commingle, intermingle: ne tuas sordes cum clarissimorum virorum splendore permisceas,: tristia laetis,: geminas e sanguine matris permistura domos,: acerbitas morum ne vino quidem permista,.—Of language: quibus (intervallis longis et brevibus) implicata atque permixta oratio,.—
In partic., to confound, disturb, throw into confusion, : omnia,; cf.: omnia divina humanaque jura permiscentur,: domum,; : Graeciam,: omnia gravi timore,.—Hence, permixtus, a, um (perh. not permistus in class. Lat.), P. a.
Promiscuous, confused: permixta caedes,; : mores,disordered, disorderly,.—
Filled: permixtus maerore,fin.—Adv.: per-mixtē, confusedly, promiscuously, ; .
la:verb:permisceo.inflection: scŭi, stum, and xtum, 2, v. a.

la:verb:permulceo.gloss: to touch or rub gently, stroke, caress
senses: to touch or rub gently, stroke, caress
la:verb:permulceo.html:
per-mulcĕo, mulsi, sum, and ctum, 2, v. a.,
to rub gently, to stroke.
Lit.: ut pulverem Manibus isdem, quibus Ulixi saepe permulsi, abluam, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 90 Rib.); so, aliquem manu, Ov F. 4, 551: capite permulso, Varr. ap. P.: barbam,: alicui malas,: comas,.—
Transf.
To touch gently: aram flatu permulcet spiritus austri, blows softly upon, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 44, 114: arteriae leni voce permulsae,: medicatā lumina virgā,; .—
To soften: cera picem lenitate permulcet,.—
Trop.
To charm, please, delight, flatter, fondle: sensum voluptate,: aures,: aliquem permulcere atque allicere,: aures cantibus,: his verbis vacuas permulceat auris,.—
To soothe, appease, allay, tame: eorum animis permulsis et confirmatis,: pectora dictis,: liberalibus verbis permulcti sunt, ap. P.: iram alicujus,: aliquem mitibus verbis,: comitate militem,: animos,: senectutem,to mitigate,.
la:verb:permulceo.inflection: mulsi, sum, and ctum, 2, v. a.

la:verb:permeo.html:
per-mĕo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to go or pass through, to cross, traverse.
Lit.: Euphrates mediam Babylonem permeans,: Alpheus in eā insulā sub ima maria permeat,: in quos (barbaros) saxa et hastae longius permeabant, quam ut contrario sagittarum icto adaequarentur, traversed too much space, i. e. went too far in reaching them, etc., : Ister permeat orbem,: dum littera nostra Tot maria ac terras permeat,: permeato amne,.—Impers. pass.: iter, quo ab usque Pontico mari in Galliam permeatur,.—
Transf., to go forward, go on: naviter et sine ullis concessationibus,.—
Trop., to penetrate, pervade: quod quaedam animalis intellegentia per omnia ea permeet et transeat,.

la:verb:permoveo.gloss: to move, shake up or stir up thoroughly, agitate
senses: to move, shake up or stir up thoroughly, agitate
to move deeply; stir or rouse up, overrule, excite, arouse; upset; influence, sway, induce, persuade
la:verb:permoveo.html:
per-mŏvĕo, mōvi, mōtum, 2, v. a.,
to move or stir up thoroughly.
Lit. (very rare): mare permotum ventis,: terram sarritione,: resinae uncias tres dolio immergunt et permovent,to stir about, shake up,.—
Trop.
Of the mind, to move deeply; to stir up, rouse up, excite; to influence, lead, induce, persuade, prevail on, etc. (freq. and class.): si quem aratorum fugae, calamitates, exilia, suspendia denique non permovent,: in commovendis judicibus, iis sensibus permoveor,: mentem judicum,: aliquem pollicitationibus,: labore itineris,: sive iracundiā, sive dolore, sive metu permotus,: his rebus adducti atque auctoritate Orgetorigis permoti,: plebes dominandi studio permota,: mente permotus, in an ecstasy or frenzy, .—
To stir up, rouse, raise, excite a passion (post-Aug. and rare): invidiam, misericordiam, metum et iras,.

la:noun:permixtio.html:
permixtĭo (permistĭo), ōnis, f.
id.
.
A mixing together; concr., ingredients mixed together, a mixture, . —
In partic., a mixture, . —
A confusion, disturbance: rei publicae permixtio,: dissensio civilis, quasi permixtio terrae,

la:noun:permutatio.html:
permūtātĭo, ōnis, f.
permuto
.
A changing, altering, change, alteration: magna rerum,: temporum,; : defensionis,: vicissitudinum,.—
An interchanging, barter, exchanging, exchange: mercium,: partim emptiones, partim permutationes,: haec res permutationem non recipit,: rerum,: captivorum,; . —Of exchanging money, negotiating a bill of exchange, ; .—
A substitution.
In rhet., of one expression for another, permutation, .—
Of one person for another: similis si permutatio detur,.

la:adj:permirus.html:
per-mīrus, a, um, adj.,
very wonderful

(class.): ut mihi permirum videatur, quemquam exstare, etc.,: illud vero mihi permirum accidit, fuisse, etc.,.—In tmesi: per mihi mirum visum est,.

la:noun:permissio.html:
permissĭo, ōnis, f.
permitto
.
In gen., a giving up, yielding, ceding to another's will and pleasure; an unconditional turrender, .—
A rhet. figure, in which a thing is committed to the decision of one's opponent, permission, ; ; .—
In partic., leave, permission (very rare for permissus): mea permissio mansionis tuae,: sine permissione Dei diabolus nocere non potest,.

la:adj:permodestus.html:
per-mŏdestus, a, um, adj.,
very moderate, very modest: homo,; , b, 3: verba sensu permodesto,.
